intro: The structural multi-quarter thesis is strengthening this week despite the FOMC shock. Three new developments since June 17 reinforce the long-horizon picture: (1) SK Hynix confirmed HBM4E sample shipments for June 2026 — the HBM technology roadmap is accelerating beyond consensus, with the product-cycle advantage extending into 2028; (2) The Iran ceasefire formal signing June 19 removes the most persistent inflation overhang driving Warsh's hawkish dots — the medium-term macro sequence (Hormuz → oil lower → CPI relief → DXY peaks) is now underway on a 6–8 week timeline; (3) NVDA held above $200 through the most hawkish FOMC since 2022 and delivered the first 50-DMA recovery close on June 18 — institutional conviction in the AI capex thesis is demonstrated, not claimed. Bitcoin's near-term stop execution (Day 2 active) is a cyclical disruption in the structural adoption thesis, not a reversal — the fixed-supply, widening-institutional-access story spans halvings, not FOMC meetings. The FOMC-driven dislocations in NVDA, META, MSFT, GOOGL, and AMZN are multi-quarter accumulation opportunities. Use Juneteenth as a forced patience moment — the thesis doesn't change in a day.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: The toll road on AI compute — FOMC-driven multiple discounts are structural accumulation windows.
ideas.why: NVDA's $25B bond raise ($85B orders, 3.4x oversubscribed) is management's public declaration of AI capex continuity regardless of the rate environment. Jensen Huang's 18-day Taiwan–South Korea trip ($150B annual spending commitment, Korean robotics/AI/memory deals) demonstrates supply-chain construction at the multi-decade horizon. The CUDA moat, Blackwell/Vera Rubin roadmap, SK Hynix HBM4E supply locked through 2030, Apple/Google PCC (Siri via Blackwell B200), and the $299 average analyst PT create a multi-year structural bid. Warsh's hawkish dots create a near-term multiple headwind (higher discount rate on ~30x P/E), not a change in the trajectory of AI capex. The $195–$215 zone is the structural accumulation window.
ideas.driver: Hyperscaler + sovereign AI capex compounding through 2028+; inference demand following training ramp; HBM4E supply locked through multi-year SK Hynix partnership; Vera Rubin rack-scale systems entering production 2026–2027.
ideas.risk: Custom ASICs (hyperscaler in-house silicon) erode NVDA's H100/B200 share faster than expected; or Fed delivers multiple hikes in 2026 creating a sustained 30Y above 5.25% that compresses the AI-capex multiple sector-wide.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: HBM4E sampling confirmed June 2026 — the memory AI trade is entering its next product generation with the technology moat widening at exactly the moment the supply shortage extends through 2028.
ideas.why: SK Hynix confirmed HBM4E sample shipments 'as soon as this month' (June 2026) — approximately three weeks after Samsung's May 29 shipment, validating the technology roadmap and initiating the customer qualification process for 2027 mass production. With NVIDIA supply partnership through 2030, ~58–70% HBM market share by revenue, 72% Q1 operating margin, a PT revision cycle underway (consensus ₩2,690,000 already exceeded, ₩3.0M+ expected), a KOSPI 9,000 passive index inflow structural bid, and shareholder value enhancement program pending — this is the highest-conviction structural idea in the portfolio. The July 29 Q2 earnings call is the next catalyst for the ₩3.0M+ PT revision.
ideas.driver: HBM4→4E product transition with SK Hynix the clear technology leader; shortage extending through 2028; NVIDIA supply lock; sell-side PT revision cycle from ₩2,690,000 to ₩3.0M–₩3.2M now underway; KOSPI 9,000 passive inflow structural bid.
ideas.risk: Samsung executes a credible HBM4E capacity ramp that captures qualification slots before SK Hynix completes customer qualification; memory industry reverts to cyclical oversupply if AI capex cycle has a digestion pause in 2027.

ideas.name: Microsoft
ideas.idea: The lowest-risk path to enterprise AI monetization — the FOMC selloff to ~$378 is a structural accumulation opportunity.
ideas.why: Microsoft's enterprise AI thesis is compounding: Azure AI workloads are inflecting, Copilot attach rates across hundreds of millions of enterprise seats are growing, and the OpenAI investment provides asymmetric exposure to frontier model development. At ~$378, the post-FOMC selloff offers a better entry than any time since the SPCX IPO briefly pulled growth capital allocation toward infrastructure narratives. The recurring-revenue enterprise model makes Microsoft the least DCF-sensitive megacap to rate uncertainty — cash flows are real, current, and contracted. The $375–$390 zone is the structural accumulation window with clear risk parameters.
ideas.driver: Azure AI workload attach rates + Copilot enterprise adoption across hundreds of millions of seats; OpenAI relationship providing frontier model access and differentiated enterprise AI capability.
ideas.risk: AI capex-to-monetization ratio deteriorates (spending accelerating faster than Azure revenue inflection); antitrust scrutiny of the OpenAI relationship complicates the enterprise AI bundle; new AI-native infrastructure narratives pull growth capital allocation away from 'old AI' incumbents.

ideas.name: Alphabet
ideas.idea: The cheapest AI full-stack at the megacap cohort's lowest multiple — search cannibalization risk is still being priced too harshly.
ideas.why: Alphabet owns Gemini (frontier models), TPUs (cost-competitive inference), Google Cloud (inflecting), and search (generating the cash to fund all of it). At ~$355 post-FOMC selloff, the forward multiple is the cheapest in the megacap cohort. If AI Overviews prove to be a moat-extender (users stay on Google longer and see more premium ad inventory), the re-rating is a multi-year compounding opportunity. Iran oil disinflation → lower DXY medium-term is a structural tailwind for Alphabet's emerging-market ad revenue. The Warsh regime creates near-term multiple compression but doesn't touch Alphabet's competitive moat or the structural ad market.
ideas.driver: TPU-driven inference cost advantage enabling competitive pricing; Gemini integration across a billion-user surface; Google Cloud AI workloads inflecting on enterprise adoption; potential search-moat expansion rather than cannibalization.
ideas.risk: Genuine query erosion to AI assistants at scale (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini own-cannibalization) compounds advertising revenue decline; antitrust remedies fracturing the search + advertising bundle; higher-for-longer rates extend the multiple compression window.

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: A generational franchise — near-term step-aside after $185 stop trigger; watch for $165–$175 stabilization base before re-engaging the 3–5 year thesis.
ideas.why: SpaceX owns the only proven reusable orbital launch system at scale, Starlink at 5M+ subscribers growing ~40% annually, Starshield national-security contracts, and the AI coding platform Cursor (Anysphere, $60B stock acquisition). The IPO at $135 raised $75B — the largest ever. The near-term step-aside (stop triggered at $174.90 June 18) is a tactical response to the FOMC hawkish repricing of an 84x-revenue multiple, not a rejection of the 3–5 year structural thesis. The structural trade: build a position at $165–$175 (after stabilization base confirmed) with a July put hedge and hold for the September 2 first earnings disclosure. December 2026 lock-up expiry is the first major supply event — the float-squeeze mechanics end there.
ideas.driver: Starlink subscriber and ARPU compounding toward a recurring-revenue connectivity utility; Starship reducing cost-to-orbit toward near-zero; Cursor AI software layer adding recurring software revenue to the infrastructure franchise; Starshield national-security base load.
ideas.risk: IPO-cycle overvaluation creates a poor structural entry if the passive bid exhausts before fundamentals support the current price level; September 2 first earnings disappoints vs $2.4T implied expectations; key-person concentration risk (Elon Musk); long lock-up period (December 9) makes early shareholders nervous.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: Structural adoption thesis intact despite near-term stop execution — re-entry at $60,000–$62,000 after two-day stabilization.
ideas.why: The June 2026 BTC stop execution (Day 2 active at $62,520) is a cyclical disruption in the structural adoption thesis, not a structural reversal. The thesis: fixed supply (21M BTC hard cap) + widening institutional access (IBIT, FBTC, BITA with $60B+ combined AUM) + corporate treasury ownership (Strategy, MicroStrategy) + halving cycle supply reduction (most recent April 2024) + Iran ceasefire → oil lower → CPI relief → DXY peaks. The IBIT 11-day outflow streak and Fear & Greed at 8 (extreme fear) are cyclical signals tied to the FOMC hawkish shock, not structural BTC demand. LTH accumulation of 125,000 BTC in June (prior data) is the smart-money signal. At the multi-year horizon, the primary driver remains the halving cycle and widening institutional access ramp. Re-entry at $60,000–$62,000 after two-day stabilization.
ideas.driver: Fixed supply meeting widening institutional access (ETFs, corporate treasuries) across halving cycles; DXY structural decline medium-term as Hormuz reopening removes oil-inflation driver; monetary policy uncertainty favoring hard assets in a 'no forward guidance' regime.
ideas.risk: Warsh actually delivers multiple hikes (not just aspirational dots), creating a multi-quarter DXY strength regime structurally bearish for BTC; IBIT outflows that sustain at $100M+/day for 10+ sessions signal institutional exit rather than cyclical rotation; Strategy BTC sales signal the corporate treasury accumulation thesis is reversing.

ideas.name: Amazon
ideas.idea: AWS AI is the cloud infrastructure winner — the post-FOMC dip to ~$183 makes the entry more attractive, not less.
ideas.why: Amazon runs the world's largest commercial cloud (AWS), is ramping Trainium/Inferentia custom silicon to reduce AI inference costs for its own and third-party workloads, and has a logistics-and-Prime flywheel that scales into robotic AI. The FOMC-driven selloff of ~3.46% on June 17 brings AMZN to ~$183 — the most attractive valuation point in the megacap cloud cohort. AWS AI workloads are inflecting: enterprise migration to cloud-native AI accelerates as the cost of inference falls via custom silicon. The SPCX/NVDA narrative temporarily obscures AMZN's AI infrastructure story, creating an entry opportunity for investors with a 2–4 year horizon. Iran ceasefire → oil lower → shipping cost inflation moderating → Amazon logistics economics improving.
ideas.driver: AWS AI workload attach rates + Trainium/Inferentia inference cost advantage enabling competitive pricing; Prime and logistics flywheel compounding at scale; Hormuz reopening reducing shipping cost inflation.
ideas.risk: Cloud spending deceleration if enterprise IT budgets tighten in a higher-rate environment; competitive pressure from Azure and Google Cloud on AI workload share; Trainium/Inferentia custom silicon ramp extends timelines longer than expected.
